articles.title: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay
articles.summary: Ismail Kartal tells reporters he will leave ‘never to return’ Club president: ‘I am his senior, I told him to continue’ The Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club…
body: Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks.

Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added.

“I just spoke to Ismail Kartal. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure,” he said. Asked whether the manager had told him he would stay, Yildirim said: “There’s no need for him ‌to say that he’d continue. I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s ​it. We are a family.”

Kartal, who spent a decade at Fenerbahce as a player, coached the club in 2014-15, then on an interim basis in 2021-22 before returning for a full ⁠campaign in 2023-24. He was the assistant manager at Fenerbahce the ​past two ​times the club won ​the Turkish title, and returned for a fourth ​managerial spell in ‌June.

articles.title: Champions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past Leipzig
articles.summary: Bayern Munich 5-0 Bodø/Glimt, Como 4-1 Leipzig. Lens win 3-2 at Slavia Prague with last-gasp double. Bayern Munich opened their Champions League campaign with a 5-0 thrashing of Norway’s Bodo/Glimt.
body: The six-times winners were frustrated before half-time by Bodo/Glimt but cruised once Jamal Musiala smashed in the opener two minutes into the second period and the floodgates opened.

Harry Kane headed the second on the hour – his 34th goal in 39 Champions League appearances for Bayern – and Alphonso Davies made it 3-0 with a powerful half-volley. With Vincent Kompany’s side in full flow, Michael ‌Olise completed the scoring with a superb late brace.
Cesc Fàbregas’s Como impressed on their debut in Europe’s premier club competition, crushing RB Lepzig 4-1.

Goals from Croatia midfielder Martin Baturina, Greece forward Tasos Douvikas and Senegal’s Assane Diao put Como in control. Serbia midfielder Andrija Maksimović pulled a goal back for Leipzig, before Maximo Perrone sealed a 4-1 victory late on in a dream night in northern Italy.

articles.title: Davies sinks world champion Wu at English Open
articles.summary: World champion Wu Yize is knocked out of the English Open in the third round as he loses 4-1 to Liam Davies, who faces fellow Welshman Mark Williams next.
body: World champion Wu Yize fell in the third round of the English Open as Liam Davies scored an eye-catching 4-1 victory in Brentwood.

Welsh prospect Davies, 20, opened up a 3-0 lead on his way to the first ranking event quarter-final of his career, helped by a break of 105 in the second frame, then completed his victory as China's Wu struggled to find his dynamic best form.
Tantalisingly, Davies will face compatriot Mark Williams, the three-time world champion, in the last eight on Friday evening.
Williams, still a major force on the baize at the age of 51, had breaks of 76, 103 and 63 in a late-night 4-1 victory over England's Barry Hawkins.

articles.title: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return
articles.summary: It was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points…
body: It was also a night for cold, hard reality. Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.

Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.

articles.title: Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter
articles.summary: Deal would value club at around £5bn. Walter is seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers. Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are closing in on an agreement to buy out co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in a deal that would see the pair make a profit on their investment and value the…
body: On-off discussions between the two ownership groups over a potential sale have been taking place for the last two years, but intensified last month as a result of Mark Walter seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers following a US federal investigation over alleged tax fraud.

Walter, Boehly and Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss all own 12.8% of Chelsea following their joint £2.5bn purchase of the club with Clearlake from Roman Abramovich four years ago, in a deal in which the new owners commit to spending a further £1.75bn on the club.

In a statement issued to Bloomberg a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close. Boehly is also expected to sell as he is a long-time investment partner of Walters. Wyss’s position is unconfirmed.

“This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him,” a spokesperson for Walter said.

articles.title: Texas baseball: Exhibition, SEC schedules set for Longhorns ahead of 2027 season
articles.summary: The Texas baseball team will play ball this fall. On Thursday, Texas announced that it will head to Round Rock's Dell Diamond on Oct. 3 for an exhibition game against Houston. The first pitch for the Longhorns and Cougars is set for 12 p.m. The nine-inning scrimmage will be UT's only fall contest.
body: Texas holds a 99-35-2 lead in its all-time series with Houston. This past March, the Cougars recorded a 9-7 win at the Longhorns' expense in Houston.

Texas reached the College World Series in 2026 as head coach Jim Schlossnagle finished up his second season with the program. The Longhorns are set to return 14 letterwinners in 2027, and UT is adding both a highly-rated transfer class and a top-five recruiting class to its roster.

Thursday's announcement about the Houston exhibition wasn't the only schedule-related news that was released by Texas this week. On Tuesday, the SEC schedule for UT was also revealed. The Longhorns will host South Carolina (March 25-27), Tennessee (April 9-11), Arkansas (April 23-25), Vanderbilt (April 30-May 2) and Texas A&M (May 14-16) this spring while also visiting LSU (March 19-21), Alabama (April 2-4), Florida (April 16-18), Oklahoma (May 7-9) and Georgia (May 20-22).

articles.title: 'A great sporting ticket' - US Open chief vows to keep day, night session format
articles.summary: US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027.
body: Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.
Players have long loved the electricity of playing night matches under the lights in the nation's biggest city.
But the tournament had already set a record with three post-2am finishes over the first six days, as well as having two other matches go past 1am.

articles.summary: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe will continue their ⁠quest to become the first American men's Grand Slam champion ⁠since Andy Roddick's 2003 triumph at Flushing Meadows as the US Open reaches its semi-final stage.
body: Shelton sent defending champion Carlos Alcaraz packing in the early ‌hours of Wednesday with the pair slugging it out in the latest-finishing match in tournament history as he reached his third major semi-final, having made the final four in the 2023 US Open and 2025 Australian Open.
"That was a war," said Shelton. "The most enjoyable match that I've had in my career."
Tiafoe recovered from two sets and ‌a break down to beat compatriot Alex Michelsen, reaching the semi-finals for a third time in a thrilling fightback.

The American has provided treasured memories ​for the home fans in New York, from his dragon-slaying defeat of Rafael Nadal en route to the 2022 semi-final, ​to his blockbuster win over compatriot Shelton two ‌years ago.

articles.title: York Knights finish maiden Super League season with thrashing of Bradford
articles.summary: York saw off bottom club Bradford 35-16 in their final match of the regular Super League campaign at the LNER Community Stadium, where Paul Vaughan slotted over a late drop goal on his farewell appearance before retirement.
body: The Knights - looking to solidify a 10th-place finish in their debut Super League season - had Scott Galeano sent to the sin bin after just 13 minutes following a tip tackle on Phoenix Steinwede, with Bulls then having a try for full-back Caleb Aekins ruled out for a forward offload.

Ryan Sutton made the breakthrough to score the opening try for Bradford after 17 minutes, with Chris Atkin slotting over the extras. The lead, though, was short-lived as Galeano marked his return to the action by showing quick feet to then dive over.
Ben Jones-Bishop, who was given a guard of honour ahead of making his 400th career appearance, added another try for the home side, with Cody Hunter converting for a 12-6 lead.

Bradford rallied again as Riley Dean latched on to a spilled kick to touchdown, but York responded again just before half-time as Toa Mata'afa burst down the middle to send the Knights into the break 18-12 ahead.
